title: Direct observation of photon-induced vortices in superconducting films
authors: Takeshi Jodoi, Fuminori Hirayama, Tetsuya Tsuruta, Takahiro Kikuchi, Daiji Fukuda
abstract: Nucleation of vortex-antivortex pairs (VAPs) is believed to play a central role in the photon detection mechanism of superconducting detectors; however, their direct dynamic observation has remained challenging. Here, we report the direct observation of photon-induced VAP dynamics in a current-carrying superconductor as quantized voltage signals following photon absorption. The observed signals are interpreted as discrete phase-slip events, where each vortex traversal induces a 2-pi phase change of the superconducting order parameter, resulting in a quantized voltage pulse whose time integral is given by the magnetic flux quantum. We analyze the resulting quantized signals as a function of bias current, base temperature, and input photon-number states, and find that the number of VAPs generated per absorbed photon becomes effectively stabilized under specific conditions. Under these conditions, we demonstrate photon-number-resolving capability by directly counting phase-slip-induced voltage quanta. Our results reveal a detection mechanism governed by phase dynamics rather than conventional resistive transitions. We further show that photon-number resolution emerges when the fluctuation of photon-induced vortex-antivortex pair generation becomes statistically suppressed. These findings establish a new route toward photon-number-resolving detection based on phase-slip counting and open opportunities for high-speed superconducting detectors for quantum optics and photonic quantum technologies.
summary: The authors report the direct observation of photon-induced vortex-antivortex pair dynamics in superconducting films, interpreting the resulting quantized voltage signals as discrete phase-slip events. By analyzing the statistical fluctuations of these VAPs, they demonstrate that the device achieves photon-number resolution by linking absorbed photons directly to countable flux quanta changes.
main_problem: The study aims to directly observe photon-induced vortex-antivortex pair (VAP) dynamics in superconducting films and demonstrate a mechanism for photon-number resolution.
main_result: The detection signal is governed by quantized voltage pulses resulting from discrete phase-slip events, allowing for the direct counting of absorbed photons under specific operating conditions.
method: Measurements involve irradiating a superconducting film with laser pulses while monitoring the resulting quantized voltage signals using SQUID readout.
model_or_system: The physical system is a bilayer superconducting film patterned into a strip (VBD) operated in a current-carrying state. The mechanism relies on non-equilibrium phase dynamics where photon absorption triggers VAP nucleation, leading to $2\pi$ phase slips.
key_observables: Quantized voltage pulses whose time integral equals integer multiples of the magnetic flux quantum ($\Phi_0$), and the second-order correlation function ($g^{(2)}_{	ext{VAP}}$).
important_parameters: Bias current ($I_b$), base temperature ($T_b$), input photon number ($\mu_{	ext{in}}$), and the superconducting phase slip mechanism.
main_assumptions: The detection process is fundamentally governed by discrete phase-slip events rather than conventional resistive transitions, and PNR capability emerges when VAP generation fluctuations are statistically suppressed (approaching Poissonian statistics).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate comparisons between resistive vs. phase-slip detection modes; show the temperature dependence of critical current ($I_c$); display pulse height distributions showing discrete peaks; and finally, present $g^{(2)}$ measurements confirming Poissonian statistics for photon counting.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform (VBD) and contrasting its mechanism with conventional detectors. It then details the measurement of quantized voltage signals ($\Phi_0$ quantization). Finally, it uses correlation functions ($g^{(2)}$) to demonstrate that under optimized conditions, the VAP generation statistics match the incident photon statistics, confirming PNR.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization of quantum light detection based on fundamental superconducting phase dynamics (phase slips), offering a novel pathway for high-speed quantum optical detectors distinct from standard resistive or quasiparticle tunneling mechanisms.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of photon detection mecha- nisms: (a) conventional resistive detection, in which pho- ton absorption generates many vortex–antivortex pairs, re- sulting in heating, normal-domain formation, and a resistive response; and (b) VAP-mediated phase-slip detection (VBD in this work), in which only a few VAPs are generated and directly detected as quantized voltage pulses. The lower pan- els illustrate the transient suppression and recovery of the superconducting order parameter ∆(t) and the correspond- ing phase evolution ϕ(t) associated with discrete phase-slip events.

Figure 2(a) shows the readout circuit for the VBD, where the VBD and an inductor with inductance L are shunted by a resistor Rs. A bias current Ib is supplied to the VBD from an external current source. The VBD is cooled to a base temperature Tb < Tc so that under equilibrium conditions, almost all of Ib flows through the VBD. The VBD is optically coupled to a fiber, and a laser pulse with an average photon number µin is delivered to it through the fiber. The wavelength of the incident pho- tons was 1526 nm.
